brief:
Pep Guardiola, Manchester City's manager, called on the world to "disobey horror" over Gaza and expressed support for the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement, Al Jazeera English reported. The football icon said it is more urgent than ever to demand an end to what he characterized as Israel's "apartheid, colonialism and occupation."

Guardiola's statement aligns the prominent sports figure with Palestinian solidarity campaigns. His public backing of BDS, a movement that Israeli officials and Western governments have criticized as antisemitic, represents a rare intervention by a high-profile coach in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
dek: Football icon says it is more urgent than ever to demand an end to Israel's 'apartheid, colonialism and occupation'.
title: Guardiola urges global action against Gaza violence, backs boycott movement
